observations: Photo 0 shows two large bellhousing/gearbox assemblies side-by-side, with clutches/flywheel areas visible; wiring/hoses and internal components are exposed.
Photo 1 shows the underside/side of a gearbox area with multiple electrical connectors/wires and a sensor/solenoid-looking cluster.
Photo 2 shows a complete gearbox assembly on the floor with external housings, hoses/wiring, and mounting points visible.
No clear Toyota model year, gearbox code, or transmission type label is readable in any photo.

claims.claim: automatic gearbox and manual gearbox for toyota corolla, carry, hilux,...
claims.evidence: Photos show gearbox assemblies but do not show readable Toyota model/gearbox code, nor clear identification of whether these are automatic vs manual, or which vehicle fitment.

risks.risk: Transmission type mismatch (automatic vs manual) or wrong variant for the specific Corolla/Carry/Hilux model/engine.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the transmission identification plate/stamping (gearbox code) and the VIN/engine code of the donor car, plus a photo showing the shifter/selector linkage type (for auto) or clutch linkage (for manual).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: wrong fitment/unknown type (treated as not guaranteed to fit).

risks.risk: Unknown condition (may be incomplete, missing solenoids/sensors, or damaged internals).
risks.proof: Ask for a video of the gearbox being tested (bench test or at least power-on scan for auto) and a checklist photo showing all external parts included (starter ring area, sensors/solenoids, harness connectors).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: not confirmed working / may be incomplete.

risks.risk: Electrical/solenoid/sensor issues (especially for automatic) due to exposed wiring/connectors and unknown history.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of every connector and sensor/solenoid on the unit, and a scan report (OBD) showing transmission fault codes (if auto).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: electrical faults possible (treated as not working).

risks.risk: Missing or worn clutch/flexplate/torque converter components (depending on auto/manual).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo showing the torque converter/flexplate area (auto) or clutch cover/pressure plate interface (manual), and confirm what is included.

risks.risk: Shipping/handling damage or leaks (seals, mounts, cooler lines).
risks.proof: Ask for photos of all seals/gaskets and any fluid residue/leaks, plus confirmation of whether the unit was drained and capped.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: may require reseal/repair.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the transmission code/ID plate or stamped code on the gearbox housing (the part that determines exact fitment).
Photo showing whether it is automatic or manual (e.g., selector/valve body area for auto; clutch linkage/throwout area for manual).
Video/clip of a functional test (or at minimum: proof it was removed from a running vehicle) and any scan report for automatic.
List of included parts (harness, sensors/solenoids, cooler lines, starter ring/flexplate/torque converter or clutch components) with photos of each.
response.reason: The photos show gearbox assemblies, but they do not provide readable identification (gearbox code/fitment) or confirm automatic vs manual and working condition. Without that, a worst-case price cannot be reliably set.
